newsitem.title: USA: First Bank System wins Visa contract.
newsitem.headline: First Bank System wins Visa contract.

text.p: First Bank System Inc., the largest issuer of Visa corporate and purchasing cards in the world, said Monday it has been selected by Lockheed Martin Corp. as its exclusive provider of Visa corporate cards.
The award of a five-year contract is expected to include 85,000 cards with an anticipated annual spending of $600 million, or nearly $3 billion over the length of the contract.
The value of the contract was not disclosed.
The contract was awarded to First Bank as a result of a competitive bidding process.
First Bank, based in Minneapolis, currently provides a corporate card programme for Lockheed Martin.
Lockheed Martin, based in Bethesda, Md., expects this programme to save the company about $10 million in administrative costs over the life of the contract.
First Bank, a regional bank holding company with assets of $36 billion, said it will have a dedicated team to support the account.

Lockheed Martin develops and makes advanced-technology products and services for aeronautics, electronics, energy and environment, and telecommunications. On Thursday, it announced plans to acquire Northrop Grumman Corp. in an $11.6 billion deal.
First Bank's stock fell 56 cents to $89.81, while Lockheed Martin rose 56 cents to $99.69 on the New York Stock Exchange.
